clue.text: Flaw, one of many found in computer

definitions.meaning: a small nick or broken-off piece in china or a blade is a flaw

definitions.text: one of many found in computer
definitions.meaning: a microprocessor or memory component; a computer holds many of these silicon parts

explanation.surface: A defect turns out to be one of the many components inside a computer.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a small defect such as a nick in a cup; the other is the silicon integrated circuit used in electronics.

clue.text: One who puts up traveller

definitions.meaning: someone who raises something, as one who hikes prices or rents
a walker travelling on foot across country

explanation.surface: Someone offering lodging to a passing traveller.
explanation.definitionFit: To hike is to raise (prices, a hem), so one who does it puts things up; it is also a rambler on foot.

clue.text: Carrying some weight, heaving adult's powerful

indicators.note: heaving here means throwing out, so a letter is thrown out of the word for a pot belly

parts.note: paunchy describes someone with a pot belly, carrying extra weight
A is the abbreviation for adult, as on a film certificate; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: A heavy adult panting and heaving is still strong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heaving' looks like breathing hard, but it means throwing out: the A goes from PAUNCHY.
explanation.definitionFit: Punchy writing or a punchy drink is forceful and effective, a synonym of strong.

clue.text: This compiler's about to open item of luggage to get tunic

indicators.note: to open means to go into, so the reversed pronoun is set inside the luggage word

parts.note: a case is a suitcase, an item of luggage

indicators.note: about tells us to turn the setter's contraction round

parts.note: the setter refers to themselves; 'this compiler is' becomes I'M

explanation.surface: The setter is about to unpack a suitcase to fetch a tunic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns I'M into MI, which goes into CASE.
explanation.definitionFit: A camise is a loose shirt or smock, a type of light tunic.

clue.text: Card's lead from player expressed as mathematical term

indicators.note: a card's lead is the first one played, so the opening letter of the word is taken

parts.note: of can mean from, as in 'of noble birth'
an actor is a player on the stage

explanation.surface: A bridge player leads a card that turns out to be expressed in maths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' looks like a bridge term but asks for the first letter of 'Card's'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cofactor is a quantity used in matrix algebra, so it is a technical term in mathematics.

clue.text: Left to feed crazed marmoset, producing chaos

indicators.note: to feed means to go into, so the letter is put inside the jumbled monkey
crazed signals that the letters of the monkey's name are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone leaves food for a frenzied little monkey, and pandemonium follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crazed' shuffles MARMOSET to MAESTROM; 'to feed' puts L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A maelstrom is a powerful whirlpool and figuratively a scene of turmoil, so a synonym for confusion.

clue.text: Costly safari — it is arranged in a competent way

indicators.note: arranged means the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: An expensive safari is organised well.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder stops at 'it'; 'is' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something satisfactorily means doing it well enough, which is an adequate or capable manner.

clue.text: Rascal screened by broadcaster is not hiding much

indicators.note: screened by means covered or enclosed by, so the rascal goes inside the broadcaster

parts.note: Sky is a British satellite TV broadcaster
an imp is a mischievous child, a rascal

explanation.surface: A villain shown on TV is barely concealing anything.
explanation.walkthrough: Sky is a British satellite television company; 'screened' suggests TV but means enclosed.
explanation.definitionFit: A skimpy outfit is scanty and revealing, so it covers little of the body.

clue.text: One training emu to fly is involved in an uphill struggle

definitions.note: taken literally, a climb up a mountain

indicators.note: to fly here means to send the letters flying into a new order

explanation.surface: Teaching a flightless emu to fly is a hopeless task.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is read literally: climbing is a struggle uphill.
explanation.definitionFit: Climbing peaks is literally a hard slog upward, a playful reading of the idiom for a difficult task.

clue.text: To get old property presents repercussions

parts.note: to knock on is an informal idiom for growing old, as in 'he's knocking on a bit'
personal effects are a person's belongings or property

explanation.surface: Inheriting ancestral property brings consequences.
explanation.definitionFit: Knock-on effects are secondary consequences that follow from an action, i.e. its indirect results.

clue.text: Mostly lacking in strength, second-rate branch

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word is kept, its last letter dropped

parts.note: limp means floppy, without firmness or strength
B grade is second class or second-rate

explanation.surface: A weak, inferior bough on a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A limb is a large bough of a tree, the same thing as a main arm of it.

clue.text: Renovating manor, smart of queen, perhaps

indicators.note: renovating means remaking, so the letters of the house are rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: chic means stylish or smart

explanation.surface: A stylishly refurbished manor house fit for royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Renovating' turns MANOR into MONAR; 'perhaps' marks the queen as one example of a sovereign.
explanation.definitionFit: Monarchic means relating to a sovereign ruler, and a queen is one such ruler.

clue.text: Asian food starts to seem highly important around America

indicators.note: around means the initials are placed around the country's abbreviation
starts to means the opening letter of each following word is taken

explanation.surface: An eastern dish appears to be very significant across the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: The initials S, H, I sit around US.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is a Japanese dish of vinegared rice with fish, an example of food from Asia.

clue.text: The old line fixed in a railway at regular intervals

parts.note: ye is an archaic form of 'the', as in Ye Olde Tea Shoppe

indicators.note: fixed in means set inside, so the line letter goes into the railway abbreviation

explanation.surface: An old track laid on a railway, with trains running on a timetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something happening annually recurs once each twelve months, which is a fixed recurring schedule.

clue.text: Unhesitatingly partial to alcohol

parts.note: to be partial to something is to like it
a shot is a small measure of spirits

explanation.surface: Someone who readily admits to a fondness for drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something like a shot means doing it at once, eagerly and without any delay.

clue.text: Upright family rejected covering up difficult situation

indicators.note: covering up means the reversed family surrounds the tight spot
rejected means sent back, so the word for family reads backwards

parts.note: a brood is a family of young children
a jam is a tight spot or predicament

explanation.surface: A principled family disowned for hushing up a scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upright' looks like a description of the family's morals, but it is the definition: a vertical post. 'rejected' reverses the family; 'covering up' wraps it round the predicament.
explanation.definitionFit: A door jamb is the vertical post at the side of a doorframe, so a vertical member in carpentry.

clue.text: Detectives comb southern ditches

parts.note: DIs are Detective Inspectors
to card wool is to comb it out

explanation.surface: Police searching drainage channels in the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ditches' looks like a noun for channels, but it is the verb meaning gets rid of.
explanation.definitionFit: To ditch something is to throw it away, a synonym for getting rid of unwanted items.

clue.text: Awkwardly strains to comprehend king's ancient language

indicators.note: to comprehend can mean to include or contain, so the king's letter goes inside
awkwardly signals that the letters are put in a clumsy new order

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king; the 's stands for 'has'

explanation.surface: A student struggles to understand a monarch's old tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comprehend' means understand on the surface but contain here: STRAINS rearranged holds K.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanskrit is the classical tongue of India, used in Hindu scripture for millennia.

clue.text: English couple leaving somewhere to sit for animal's home

indicators.note: leaving means the pair of letters departs from the seat word

parts.note: a settee is a sofa, somewhere to sit
a pair of Es, E being the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: An English pair get up from a seat to visit an animal's lair.
explanation.definitionFit: A sett is a badger's burrow, the den where that creature lives.

clue.text: Blue, extremely shabby clothing for dog

indicators.note: clothing means wrapping around, so the outer letters enclose the dog
extremely means the outer letters of the word are used

parts.note: a mutt is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: A sad dog in very scruffy coat.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue jokes or films are risqué or obscene, matching the sense of indecent.

clue.text: Deli's in trouble after variable returns

indicators.note: after places the scrambled shop after the variable letter

parts.note: Y is a variable in algebra

indicators.note: in trouble signals that the letters are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: A delicatessen in difficulties after changeable takings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' reads as a verb on the surface but is a plural noun for income; 'in trouble' rearranges the shop's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Yields are the profits or income from an investment, matching returns as a noun.

clue.text: Some drunk, noticeably free from restraint

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few people are visibly intoxicated and unrestrained.
explanation.definitionFit: To untie a knot is to loosen and release what it binds, so to liberate.

clue.text: After time, that man thanks foreign character

indicators.note: after time means the following pieces come once the time letter is written

parts.note: he is the pronoun for that man
ta is British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: A man gives thanks to a foreigner after some time.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet, so a letter from a non-English script.

clue.text: Plied with gin, coerce warden

indicators.note: plied means twisted together like strands of yarn, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Getting a prison guard drunk to pressure them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plied with gin' reads as getting someone drunk, but 'Plied' twists GIN and COERCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A concierge is a caretaker or porter in charge of a building, essentially its keeper.

clue.text: One competed, being overtaken by climber

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
vied means competed

explanation.surface: A runner in a race is passed by a mountaineer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climber' suggests a mountaineer, but it is the plant ivy.
explanation.definitionFit: A wall that ivy has grown over is covered by that trailing plant.

clue.text: Pinch hip struggling with girdle made of fine fibre

definitions.note: of good moral fibre, i.e. of sound character

indicators.note: struggling signals the letters being wrestled into a new order

explanation.surface: A tight corset digs into someone's hip as they fight with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fine fibre' suggests cloth, but means moral fibre.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with strong moral fibre has firm ethical standards and integrity.

clue.text: Recalled heroic tale about alien stones

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the assembled letters read backwards
about means the tale goes around the alien

parts.note: a saga is a heroic Norse legend
ET is the alien from the Spielberg film

explanation.surface: A storyteller remembers an epic about an extraterrestrial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recalled' reverses the whole assembly, not just the tale: the alien sits after the first letter of the tale before everything is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Agates are banded semi-precious gems, a kind of ornamental rock.

clue.text: Bustle in need of arrangement

definitions.meaning: still to be done or organised, as on a list of tasks

explanation.surface: A busy scene still waiting to be organised.
explanation.definitionFit: A to-do is a fuss; a task 'to do' is outstanding, still waiting to be dealt with.
